titleStmt.title: Der Tempel des Ruhmes. Ein Singgedicht. Am Einzugstage der itztregierenden Königinn Juliana Maria in Copenhagen

work.title: Der Tempel des Ruhmes. Ein Singgedicht. Am Einzugstage der itztregierenden Königinn Juliana Maria in Copenhagen

history.p: Though Scheibe and his family had moved to Sønderborg in the southern part of Denmark where they established a music school for children, he still retained contact with the musical environment in Copenhagen. In 1750 a new musical society had been founded of which Scheibe was an important instigator as well as an active participant during their concert seasons. At the same time, he received commissions from the court to compose music for official events. On the 19 December 1751, the popular Queen Louise died in childbirth, and on 8 July 1752 Frederik V married Juliane Marie of Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel, the sister-in-law of Frederick the Great. Less than two weeks later, Scheibe had composed a festive cantata for the celebration of the new queen’s entry to Copenhagen which first took place on 11 October. The work was apparently rearranged, including a new section for choir ('Sangverk'), for The Musical Society where it was performed on 18 October. The libretto, written by Scheibe, was reviewed in Fortgesetzte Nachrichten six years later: 'Thunderstorm. Calm down! No weather will harm you; you see that the writer wished to have the opportunity to show off himself. The alternation between the names Juliana and Maria is merely a trifle which could, however, have been avoided.'

annot.p: 'Ved den almindelige Glæde, som i disse Dage har opfyldt denne Hovedstad, har ogsaa det høylovelige Musicaliske Selskab udi Raadhuus-Gaden distingueret sig. Efterat samtlige Lemmer af dette priiselige Selskab, deels fra Reyser, deels fra Landet, havde indfundet sig igien her i Staden, aabnede Societetet den 18 hujus igien sin i Fior med saa stor Applausu begyndte Concerts, med en prægtig Musiqve paa Hendes Majestests, vor Allernaadigste Dronnings solenne Indtog, som med Pauker og Trompeter blev opført. Den dertil forfærdigede Poesie og Musique er af den noksom bekiendte og habile Kongel. Capellmester, Hr. Scheibe, under den Titel: Der Tempel des Ruhms, en Singgedicht, paa det netteste udført. Og har Verket ey allene ved de mangfoldige derudi forekommende Forandringer, men ogsaa formedelst et derved anbragt sangverk, fortient et almindeligt Bifald.'

annot.p: 'Es donnert. Nur ruhig! euch schadet kein Wetter, merkt man, dass der Hr. Verfasser der Musik hat Gelegenheit machen wollen sich zu zeigen. Die Abwechselung der Namen Juliana und Maria ist zwar nur eine Kleinigkeit, hätte aber doch vermieden werden können.'

incipText.p: Nach dunkeln Wolken strahlt die Sonne
Ja ja! man singe nur von Lust und Wonne
Zufrieden, in süssem in heitrem Vergnügen
Doch wie? hier kommt die Zeit
Die Wahrheit strahlt aus ihren Blicken
Monarch! wenn einst die späten Zeiten
Wie? was ist doch mit mir geschehn?
In Friedrichs Schatten will ich wohnen
Verwundernd sahen wir den prächtgen Einzug an
Der Stammbaum verneue sich jährlich entzückend!

physDesc.watermark: at least two distinct watermarks are found: 1) a crowned coat-of-arms of Amsterdam set between two lions (similar Heawood:415, dated to around 1725); 2) with the countermark 'IH' or 'HI', (J. Honig); and possibly a third with the countermark 'ISRB' which is also found in SchW B2:430, composed in January 1752. Paper of a fairly dense quality.
physDesc.physMedium: In 2o, upright format consisting of 5, 3, 4, 5, 3, 5, 3, 5, 3 and 4 nested bifolios; title page (fol. 1r; p. [1]), list of instruments and characters (fol. 1v; p. [2]), music (fols. 2r–79v, numbered 3–158) in ink; in all 79 folios. Hand-ruled paper, 22–25 staves (7 mm; single rastrum used) in light brown ink and music in black ink. Score contains a few corrections or changes, all made in the same ink as the autograph; bar numbers added in pencil, presumably during the production of a new full score in 1943 (‘Egne Afskrifter’).

physDesc.condition: restored, presumably in 1960s including a new half-binding with the original leather spine including title and composer’s name gold-tooled on coloured paper pasted on to the new; tightly bound affecting margins.
physDesc.physMedium: Source contains two works, the first of which is SchW B2:430 (pp. 1−104) followed by the present one, SchW B2:439 (pp. 105−58). The front paste-down has in addition to shelf marks been stamped 'DET STORE KONGELIGE BIBLIOTHEK' and 'BIBLIOTECA REGIA HAFNIENSIS', '63' added in red crayon, and a label, 'WEYSES SAMLING | DET KGL. BIBLIOTEK', pasted on the inside.
